sc370441b13a61c: Kubernetes Default Scheduler enforces strict GPU integration, which prevents SNOW sequenced training - migration of inference flow lines - trainers and inference engines must share the same GPU. Hami solves this problem through virtualization GPU resources (vGPU), enabling multiple containers in the same Pod to share a single GPU. It is integrated with kube-schedulers without any need for modification of application codes and fully compatible with the wider automatic stretching ecology.

s2d4a4f12c75c67: On Saturday morning, the gypsy filter suddenly burst into fire three hours ago and the flow rose to a factor of three times more than local capacity. Auto-extrusion initially supported the flow, but the surge in GPU demand subsequently triggered a limit; teams had to catch up with saturation before the heat subdued. SNOW then extended its load elasticity to cloud service providers via a single Gitops stream, using the same Helm Charts, where all clusters pulled their tasks directly from the central RabbitMQ team — the entire process was cut off by zero. Finally, it managed to eliminate seven times the peak traffic, taking full advantage of the business opportunity.

s5db00ac06d6cf9: The cloud-native transition of SNOW Corp. demonstrates how to combine Kubernetes with the wider CNCF ecology, overcoming the fundamental limitations of GPU production and observability at extreme scales. By introducing Hami GPU sharing, and using active self-defined indicators to enhance KEDA, SNOW, from passive manual operations to predictive automation. This architecture not only allows the platform to absorb 700% of the peak volume of traffic that has been uninterruptedly mixed environmental expansion, but also achieves significant improvements in cost efficiency, reliability and operating speed.
